Founder Mike Wiacek cites Stairwell research that each published sample hides an average of 2.4 undocumented variants, arguing that alert-and-close triage leaves the bulk of a campaign undetected as attackers ship AI-generated variants at scale to evade signature-based defenses.

title: Cyberattacks hit water facilities in seven states across the US
blurb: The FBI issued a warning after water and wastewater facilities in seven states reported intrusions, part of a broader campaign targeting the sector's often under-secured operational technology and internet-exposed HMIs. Operators should inventory internet-facing control systems, enforce MFA and unique credentials on remote access, and segment OT from IT networks, since many affected utilities run legacy SCADA with default or shared passwords.

title: Californians' data deletion requests, DROP, become enforceable Aug. 1
blurb: California's Delete Request Opt-out Platform (DROP) became enforceable on Aug. 1, requiring the state's roughly 600 registered data brokers to honor consumer deletion requests within 45 days or face fines of $200 per day per affected resident. About 350,000 Californians have signed up since January to submit a single request that removes their personal data across all registered brokers instead of contacting each one individually.

title: A deep dive into Nvidia's Vera CPU and the Olympus cores that power it
blurb: Nvidia detailed its Vera CPU and the custom Arm-based Olympus cores behind it, packing 88 cores, 176 threads, up to 1.5 TB of memory, and 1.8 TB/s of NVLink bandwidth to feed its next-generation Rubin accelerators. The custom-core approach signals Nvidia moving further away from off-the-shelf Arm Neoverse designs, tightening its grip on the full rack and pressuring Intel and AMD in datacenter CPUs.

title: CISA Alert: Water Sector PLC Targeting
blurb: CISA warned on July 30 that threat actors are increasingly compromising internet-exposed PLCs in the water and wastewater sector, changing device passwords and IP addresses to lock out operators and force boil-water notices and manual operation. The alert names Rockwell Automation, Siemens, and Schneider Electric equipment and flags operator-installed cellular modems as an undocumented blind spot, and it directs utilities to pull OT off the internet and route remote access through VPNs or gateways.

title: Microsoft brings a long awaited "game changer" Windows 11 tool for IT admins
blurb: Microsoft introduced a long-requested Windows 11 management tool aimed at IT administrators, addressing a gap admins have flagged since the OS launched. For enterprise fleets standardized on Windows 11, the addition folds a previously manual or third-party task into native tooling, reducing reliance on separate utilities and simplifying the endpoint-management stack IT already runs through Intune and Configuration Manager.

title: Your Azure DevOps pipelines have a 2027 deadline, and the clock has just started
blurb: Microsoft deprecated the Azure DevOps issuer for workload identity federation on July 1, 2026, with full retirement set for July 1, 2027, and every Azure Pipelines Service Connection built before late 2025 needs migrating to the Entra issuer or it stops authenticating to Azure. The portal converts connections one at a time, so shops with hundreds of single-tenant connections in the public cloud will need to script the undocumented MigrateToEntraIssuer REST call to finish before the deadline.

title: Four US states rolled back or paused data center tax incentives, and nine others are weighing repeal measures, potentially adding 7% or more to equipment costs (Ann Davis Vaughan/The Information)
blurb: Four US states rolled back or paused data center tax incentives, with nine more weighing repeal measures that could add 7% or more to equipment costs. Enterprises planning on-premise or colocation buildouts in affected states face higher effective TCO on server and networking hardware, making incentive stability a new variable in site-selection and capacity-expansion decisions.

title: N-able Says Attackers Take Over N-central Servers After Initial Fix Proves Incomplete
blurb: N-able confirmed attackers exploited an authentication bypass in its N-central RMM platform to gain remote administrative access, then pivoted through the built-in Take Control tool to install persistent Cloudflare tunnels on managed endpoints. The initial fix was incomplete, so every customer must move to build 2026.3.1.7, released August 2, and separately hunt for and remove the tunnel services, which survive the N-central upgrade.

title: Iran suspected of conducting cyberattacks on US water suppliers in 45 municipalities — small towns mostly targeted, with utilities switching to manual control
blurb: Water utilities in 45 US municipalities across seven states, mostly small towns like Braham, Minnesota, reported cyberattacks on their control systems, with officials and the FBI suspecting Iranian state actors and no financial demands made. Several utilities have fallen back to manual control while they assess aging, internet-connected SCADA systems, exposing how thin the OT security budgets are at the small municipalities that run critical infrastructure.

title: Control Reliability Engineering (CRE): Applying SRE Principles to Cybersecurity Controls
blurb: Phil Venables argues that most breaches trace to security controls that were assumed operational but were actually broken or misconfigured when needed, and proposes Control Reliability Engineering (CRE) to fix it. The framework ports SRE discipline directly onto security controls: SLIs and SLOs to define a healthy control, error budgets to govern acceptable decay, and continuous control monitoring plus root-cause analysis to catch drift before an attacker does.

title: Your Azure DevOps pipelines have a 2027 deadline, and the clock has just started
blurb: Microsoft deprecated the Azure DevOps issuer for workload identity federation on July 1, 2026, giving teams until July 1, 2027 before Service Connections built on the old vstoken.dev.azure.com issuer stop authenticating to Azure. The portal migrates connections one at a time in a couple of minutes each, so orgs running hundreds will need the undocumented MigrateToEntraIssuer REST call, and only single-tenant Entra apps and Managed Identities in the public cloud are affected.

title: The development pipeline is a production system
blurb: The author argues that development pipelines deserve the same outage response as customer-facing production systems, since a broken build, failing test suite, or downed QA server stops the team from shipping just as surely as a service failure stops customers. The recommendation is to inventory every step from "customer wants something" to "delivered," from issue trackers and IDEs to CI/CD and package repositories, then treat any break in that chain as a top-priority incident rather than background toil.

title: Show HN: NixOS-DGX-Spark – Nix and NixOS on the DGX Spark
blurb: A developer released NixOS-DGX-Spark, an open-source project that brings Nix and NixOS to NVIDIA's DGX Spark and the Asus Ascent GX10, shipping USB images and a NixOS hardware module with a custom NVIDIA-optimized kernel for full GPU and Ethernet support. Teams can run the Nix dev shells and playbooks directly on stock DGX OS via nix-gl-host, or install NixOS outright for reproducible CUDA environments after a required firmware update.

title: Snapchat will no longer recommend AI slop
blurb: Snapchat updated its Spotlight recommendation algorithm to demote wholly AI-generated videos, making "AI slop" ineligible for recommendation while human-made and AI-enhanced content still qualify. The move runs counter to Meta's Vibes app, which launched a fully AI-generated feed in February, and signals that platforms are now treating authentic, human-created content as a reach advantage rather than a constraint.

title: LinkedIn offers the option to report AI slop
blurb: LinkedIn is testing an in-stream option that lets members report posts and comments as likely "AI slop," using the flags to train its detection classifiers and privately warn creators when their content reads as inauthentic. The move complicates LinkedIn's own generative-AI push, and it is replacing the "enhance your post" feature with a lighter proofreading tool as it tries to curb over-automated engagement.

title: TBM 434: How Maps Can Hide Problems
blurb: The author argues that org maps like team structures, product taxonomies, and goal hierarchies only stay reliable when strategy, structure, technology, and incentives cohere, so a map that reads cleanly can quietly paper over an incoherent org underneath. When eight teams span competing hierarchies with unclear ownership and conflicting funding bets, no single map holds and every switch forces you to reorient. The takeaway for PMs: treat a map that requires constant translation as a signal to refactor the organization, not a skill to master.

title: SEC to review Nasdaq bitcoin options approval after CME challenge
blurb: The SEC froze Nasdaq PHLX's approval of QBTC cash-settled bitcoin index options and will reconsider it after CME Group challenged the listing on jurisdictional grounds. CME argues bitcoin is a commodity, placing options on its value under CFTC authority rather than the SEC's, and the stay holds until interested parties submit comments by Aug. 24.

title: Hackers Poison Adform Script to Swap Crypto Wallet Addresses Across Customer Sites
blurb: Attackers compromised a JavaScript file served by ad-tech firm Adform, injecting code that rewrote copied and typed Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Tron wallet addresses to redirect payments to attacker-controlled destinations. Because the poisoned trackpoint-async.js loads across many unrelated client sites, the incident is a supply-chain compromise; Adform detected it on July 27, removed the code, and is telling users to clear cached scripts and verify any address before sending funds.

title: Coldcard Hardware Wallet Flaw Linked to $70 Million Bitcoin Theft in 41 Minutes
blurb: An attacker drained 1,082.65 BTC worth about $70.2 million from 1,196 Bitcoin addresses in 41 minutes on July 30, a sweep Galaxy Research tied to a firmware flaw in Coinkite's Coldcard hardware wallet that routed seed generation through a weak software PRNG instead of the hardware RNG. Coinkite shipped emergency firmware on July 31, but it cannot repair an existing seed, so owners with exposed devices must generate a new seed and move their coins.

title: How bitcoin cold wallets lost $70 million in an attack that never touched the devices
blurb: Galaxy Research found that weak seed generation, not device access, drained 1,082 BTC (about $70M) from 1,196 Coldcard wallets in a 41-minute window on July 30. An internal build flag told certain firmware to skip the dedicated hardware randomness generator, making supposedly unguessable seeds computationally enumerable and letting an attacker reconstruct private keys entirely offline. Owners cannot reliably tell whether their seeds came from vulnerable firmware, so security firms warn more wallets remain at risk.

title: SummerFi to Wind Down After Seven Years, Citing Exploit
blurb: SummerFi will wind down Summer.fi and sunset its user interface after seven years, attributing the decision to a recent exploit on its Lazy Summer Protocol that drained roughly $6M. The operator has not set a wind-down date or clarified the status of user funds, and its closure follows Zapper's planned Aug. 3 shutdown as DeFi front ends buckle under security and operating costs.

title: Bitcoin cold-wallet attack spreads to 4,500 addresses as losses near $89 million
blurb: Galaxy Research flagged a third wave of wallet sweeps exploiting weak keys from a March 2021 Coldcard firmware build, bringing total losses to 1,367 bitcoin, nearly $89 million, across 4,585 addresses. The latest wave targets smaller balances averaging a tenth of a bitcoin each and uses harder-to-trace transaction patterns, sending funds to unique pay-to-witness-script-hash outputs instead of shared collector addresses.

title: Bank of Italy research suggests stablecoins aren't necessarily cheaper for remittances
blurb: Bank of Italy tested 200 USDC transfers across 10 remittance corridors and found total costs ranged from 0.3% to nearly 9% of the amount sent, with blockchain fees a tiny fraction and exchange fees, FX spreads, and local banking charges driving the bulk. The research concludes stablecoins solve on-chain speed but not the costly last mile between crypto and local fiat.

title: Tokenized stock trading surged 288% in July, but one QQQ token drove most of it
blurb: Tokenized equity trading volume rose 288% to a record $11.3 billion in July, but a single Binance token, QQQB, generated $9.27 billion of it, roughly 82% of all tokenized-equity volume. Stripping out QQQB, whose zero maker fees and a new VIP volume multiplier drove the spike, July volume was $2.03 billion, about 30% below June's total.

title: Bitcoin mining difficulty shrinks 14% from this year's high as plunging revenues force operators to pivot
blurb: Bitcoin mining difficulty fell to 126.23 trillion, roughly 14% below its January peak and 19.1% off the November 2025 record high, as compressed revenue and capital shifting toward AI infrastructure cut network capacity. Hashprice sank to $27.66 per petahash per day in late June before recovering to $31.7, with Luxor's forward market pricing $31.85 through year-end, signaling little economic relief for remaining miners.

title: Everyone has the perps convergence backwards
blurb: In a CoinDesk opinion piece, Bitget CEO Gracy Chen argues the convergence narrative is inverted: rather than crypto maturing toward traditional finance, traditional assets are migrating onto perpetual futures, the market structure crypto invented. Real-world-asset perp volumes hit a record $211B in May 2026, roughly 16x their ~$12B level in Q4 2025, with equity perps up 121% month over month to $54B. The draw is continuous, globally accessible markets settled onchain, with no borrow desk to short and no contract to roll.

title: XRP Ledger upgrade brings back features once pulled over critical bugs
blurb: The XRP Ledger's xrpld 3.3.0 release, expected next week, asks validators to approve five amendments, including revised Batch and Permission Delegation features that were withdrawn earlier this year after researchers found bugs enabling unauthorized transactions or fee draining. Batch executes up to eight cross-account transactions atomically and Permission Delegation grants scoped signing authority, both needing 80% validator approval over two weeks to activate.

title: Marc Andreessen & Chris Dixon: Why America needs CLARITY
blurb: Marc Andreessen and Chris Dixon argued on the a16z crypto show that the CLARITY Act, the market structure bill now moving through the Senate after passing the House with bipartisan support, is once-in-a-generation legislation that would set the ground rules for where the financial system and internet get built. They frame the status quo of regulatory ambiguity as the costlier option, pushing US crypto activity offshore rather than protecting it.

title: Binance founder CZ calls for wallet diversification after $70 million Coldcard exploit
blurb: An attacker drained roughly 1,082 BTC, worth about $70 million, from 1,196 Coldcard wallets by exploiting a March 2021 firmware flaw that weakened recovery-seed randomness and let private keys be reconstructed offline. Binance founder CZ responded by urging holders to split funds across multiple wallets, reviving debate over self-custody limits after even a long-established hardware device harbored an undetected critical bug.

title: Kalshi and Polymarket’s combined volume reaches all-time high in July, surpassing $50 billion
blurb: Kalshi and Polymarket's combined trading volume topped $50B in July, an all-time monthly high for prediction markets. Polymarket US grew 54% month-over-month while the main Polymarket platform fell 26%, signaling that the CFTC-regulated US venue is absorbing demand as offshore volume cools.

title: SEC keeps Nasdaq bitcoin options on hold after granting CME review
blurb: CME Group petitioned the SEC to overturn a staff decision that conditionally approved Nasdaq PHLX's proposal to list cash-settled bitcoin index options, arguing the contracts are commodity option swaps under the CFTC's exclusive jurisdiction. The SEC granted the review and kept the approval stayed pending written statements due Aug. 24, leaving Nasdaq's index-referenced contracts blocked over the same securities-versus-commodity question that separates them from existing spot-ETF options.

title: Trump Media’s bitcoin stash may be down to loan collateral after $165 million BTC move
blurb: Trump Media moved 2,628 bitcoin worth about $165 million to Crypto.com, leaving roughly 4,261 BTC in tagged wallets that closely match the amount pledged as collateral for its convertible notes. On-chain analysts estimate the company's bitcoin bets, made near last cycle's top for $1.37 billion, have produced about $318 million in realized losses, with its Q2 10-Q the test of whether recent transfers were sales or custody moves.

title: Saylor hints at Strategy bitcoin buy after five-week pause as STRC rate stays at 12%: ‘Bitcoin Drive engaged’
blurb: Michael Saylor captioned Strategy's Sunday chart post "Bitcoin Drive engaged," signaling the firm may disclose its first bitcoin purchase in five weeks after an atypical drought that saw it instead sell shares, lift its dollar reserve to $3.75 billion, and buy back STRC. Strategy last reported holding 843,775 BTC acquired for $63.69 billion, and separately said it will keep STRC's variable annualized dividend rate at 12% for August.

title: SEC to review Nasdaq bitcoin options approval after CME challenge
blurb: The SEC froze Nasdaq PHLX's approval of QBTC cash-settled bitcoin index options to reconsider the decision after CME Group challenged it, arguing that bitcoin is a commodity whose derivatives fall under CFTC jurisdiction, not the SEC's. The outcome will define which regulator governs crypto options, and could force Nasdaq to register as a CFTC-regulated venue or redesign the contracts, with comments due by Aug. 24.

title: Bank of Italy research suggests stablecoins aren't necessarily cheaper for remittances
blurb: Bank of Italy tested 200 USDC remittances across 10 corridors and found total costs ran from 0.3% to nearly 9%, with exchange fees, FX spreads, and local banking charges, not blockchain fees, driving the expense. The research concludes stablecoins solve on-chain speed but not the costly "last mile" between crypto and local fiat, undercutting the cheaper-remittances pitch while noting always-on settlement remains a real edge.

title: AI financial advice is surprisingly good, especially if you ask right questions
blurb: A new MIT Sloan paper found that AI chatbots like GPT-5.6 and Gemini 3 Flash give financial advice that reliably builds savings buffers for most people over 30, correctly pushing them to diversify, save during working years, and cut stock exposure after 45. The models fell short on adjusting to shocks like unemployment and let portfolios drift instead of rebalancing, with advice quality varying by prompt phrasing and user financial literacy.

title: Robinhood's prediction markets revenue surged 10x+ YoY to $156M in Q2, topping stock and crypto for the first time as speculators shift to real-world event bets (Yueqi Yang/The Information)
blurb: Robinhood's prediction markets generated $156M in revenue in Q2, up more than 10x year-over-year and outpacing both equities and crypto for the first time. The shift signals that event-contract betting has become a core trading business for the brokerage, not a novelty, putting Robinhood in more direct competition with Kalshi and Polymarket for retail speculators.

title: The billion-dollar question: How will the neolabs actually make money?
blurb: The author examines how neolabs, the new wave of AI-native research startups, will convert frontier models into durable revenue rather than perpetual burn. The piece argues that API access and per-token pricing alone won't cover training costs, pushing labs toward vertical applications, enterprise contracts, and infrastructure lock-in. For fintech operators building on top of these models, the unresolved question is who ultimately captures the margin as inference costs and pricing power shift.
